title: Simulating Hybrid Analog + RISC-V Systems for HPC Applications
problem: Analog computing offers potential performance and efficiency beyond digital systems but lacks integration with complex HPC applications. Limited analog kernels cannot serve full applications; hybrid analog-digital systems are underexplored.
motivation: As digital scaling slows (beyond Moore's Law), analog computing emerges as an alternative. However, analog accelerators support only limited kernel sets. Hybrid systems could unlock analog benefits while retaining digital flexibility for complex operations.
method: Hybrid analog-digital RISC-V processors where analog accelerators serve as tightly integrated coprocessors within cores. Uses SST (Structural Simulation Toolkit) for architectural simulation. Evaluates two iterative linear solvers on hybrid systems.
key_novelty: Integrated hybrid analog-digital architecture using RISC-V as software stack foundation; architectural simulation revealing digital bottlenecks in analog-dominated workloads; insights on analog-digital balance.
contributions: Integration of analog accelerators as coprocessors within cores
Simulation framework using SST for evaluation
Analysis of iterative linear solvers on hybrid systems
Insights on balancing analog and digital operations for HPC

metrics.bottleneck: Digital operations remain bottleneck even in analog-dominated workloads

limitations: Analog devices are early-stage; limited kernel support; digital-analog interface overhead; simulation-based results (no physical implementation); scalability to large systems unclear.
